newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold easier, volume down.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold easier, volume down.

text.p: Volume on the Istanbul gold exchange eased slightly to 738 kilos on Tuesday from Monday's 783 kilos, with bank purchases sparked by a rising dollar and physical demand ahead of public holidays, dealers said.
Gold closed easier at $345.00 an ounce and 1,466,000 lira per gram, compared to $348.00 and 1,475,000 lira on Monday in line with lower levels on European markets.
"There was some physical demand from the market ahead of the holiday, but most of the day's trade was due to buying in lira terms on expectations of a stronger dollar," one dealer said.
The Turkish lira weakened to 132,470 lira to the dollar from Monday's 131,960 lira close in line with the dollar's gains in world markets.
The exchange will close for a 4-1/2-day religious holiday midday Thursday and re-open on April 22, but will again close for a national holiday on April 23 and resume trade on April 24.
Of the day's trade, 353 kilos changed hands in the morning session and 84.4 percent was conducted in lira terms.
